+# Langfuse #15208 histogram candidate
+
+## Contract
+
+Histogram membership is computed from raw numeric score values and raw range
+edges. Rounding is presentation-only. Display-edge precision increases until
+all generated edges remain distinct.
+
+## Change
+
+- Added the `0.857` regression for seven bins over `[0, 1]`.
+- Removed rounding from minimum, range, and value-to-bin calculations.
+- Added adaptive display precision for distinct labels.
+
+## Validation
+
+Narrow test command:
+
+`pnpm --filter web run test src/__tests__/server/unit/score-analytics-utils.servertest.ts`
+
+The checkout lacks `pnpm` and Node/Corepack, so the command exited before test
+collection with `/bin/bash: pnpm: command not found`.
+

+# Langfuse #15208 pivot candidate
+
+## Contract
+
+An `avg_*` subtotal or grand total is a count-weighted average when a count
+metric is present and has positive total weight. If no usable count metric is
+available, the explicit compatibility fallback is the legacy unweighted mean.
+Additive and non-average metric aggregation remains unchanged.
+
+## Change
+
+- Added unequal-group regression coverage (`1 @ 10`, `9 @ 20` => `19`).
+- Added explicit no-count fallback coverage (`10`, `20` => `15`).
+- Reused the count metric as row weights for average metrics.
+- Updated existing unequal-count expectations for subtotals and grand totals.
+
+## Validation
+
+Narrow test command:
+
+`pnpm --filter web run test src/__tests__/server/pivot-table-utils.servertest.ts`
+
+The checkout lacks `pnpm` and Node/Corepack, so the command exited before test

arguments.summary: For Langfuse score analytics, histogram bin membership must use raw numeric values and raw edges; rounding is only for display labels, whose precision must keep edges distinct. Pivot-table avg subtotals and grand totals must use count-weighted means when a usable count metric is present; when none is available (or total weight is not positive), the explicit compatibility fallback is the legacy unweighted mean. Additive and other non-average aggregations remain unchanged.
